title: Nephi urges his brothers onward
summary: Nephi urges his brothers to return to Jerusalem and keep the Lord’s commandments. He recalls Moses, the Red Sea, their fathers’ deliverance, and Pharaoh’s armies, then reminds them that an angel has spoken to them and says the Lord can deliver them.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi speaks to his brothers and urges them to go up again to Jerusalem and keep the Lord’s commandments.
Nephi invokes Moses, the Red Sea, their fathers’ passage out of captivity on dry ground, and Pharaoh’s armies drowning as reasons to be strong.
Nephi says an angel has spoken to his brothers and says the Lord is able to deliver them and destroy Laban as the Egyptians were destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi addresses his brothers while they are together.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact location of the conversation
The brothers’ appearance, age, and specific identities
Whether any recalled people or events are represented visually

spoken_dialogue.text: Let us go up again unto Jerusalem, and let us be faithful in keeping the commandments of the Lord;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: let us be strong like unto Moses;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moses, the Red Sea, and the angel are recalled in Nephi’s speech; the verses do not narrate them as present visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moses, Pharaoh’s armies, the Red Sea crossing, or an angel as present events.
Do not add lettering unless it is an exact quotation from the supplied verses.

title: Nephi enters the city
summary: Nephi and his brothers come outside Jerusalem’s walls. At night, Nephi has his brothers hide there, then creeps into the city toward the house of Laban.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi’s brothers are still angry and continue to murmur, yet follow him until they come outside Jerusalem’s walls.
It is night, and Nephi causes his brothers to hide outside the walls.
After his brothers have hidden, Nephi creeps into the city and goes toward the house of Laban.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is separated from his hidden brothers as he enters the city.
unspecified_visual_details: The brothers’ precise hiding place
The design of Jerusalem’s walls and city
The route to the house of Laban

narration.text: they were yet wroth
did still continue to murmur
they did follow me up until we came without the walls of Jerusalem.
And it was by night;
I caused that they should hide themselves without the walls.
I, Nephi, crept into the city
and went forth towards the house of Laban.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nephi’s brothers entering the city with him.

title: Nephi approaches Laban’s house
summary: Nephi is led by the Spirit without knowing beforehand what he should do. Near Laban’s house, he sees a man fallen to the earth because he is drunken with wine. Nephi comes to the man and finds that he is Laban.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi was led by the Spirit, not knowing beforehand what he should do.
As Nephi came near Laban’s house, he saw a man fallen to the earth because he was drunken with wine.
Nephi came to the man and found that it was Laban.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi approaches the fallen man near Laban’s house.
unspecified_visual_details: How the Spirit’s leading is visually represented
The precise surroundings and time

narration.text: And I was led by the Spirit, not knowing beforehand the things which I should do.
And when I came to him I found that it was Laban.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Spirit’s leading is stated, but no visible appearance of the Spirit is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Spirit a visible form.
Do not invent dialogue or additional events.

title: Nephi draws Laban’s sword
summary: Nephi draws Laban’s sword from its sheath, observes its workmanship and materials, and is constrained by the Spirit to kill Laban. He shrinks and wishes he might not slay him.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beholds a sword and draws it from its sheath; its hilt is of pure gold, its workmanship exceedingly fine, and its blade of the most precious steel.
Nephi is constrained by the Spirit that he should kill Laban; he says in his heart that he has never shed the blood of man, and shrinks, wishing he might not slay him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi holds the drawn sword and hesitates.
unspecified_visual_details: The sword’s exact design beyond the stated materials and workmanship
How the Spirit’s constraint is represented visually
Laban’s position and appearance

narration.text: And I beheld his sword, and I drew it forth from the sheath thereof;
Never at any time have I shed the blood of man.
And I shrunk and would that I might not slay him.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi’s words about never having shed human blood are inward thought, not spoken aloud.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Spirit with an appearance not stated in the verses.
Do not show Nephi killing Laban; these verses do not narrate the killing.

title: The Spirit’s words to Nephi
summary: The Spirit speaks to Nephi, saying the Lord has delivered the man into his hands. Nephi knows the man sought his life, would not hearken to the Lord’s commandments, and took their property. The Spirit commands Nephi to slay him and gives its reason concerning righteous purposes and a nation perishing in unbelief.

explicit_facts.text: The Spirit says the Lord has delivered the man into Nephi’s hands; Nephi knows the man sought to take his life, would not hearken to the Lord’s commandments, and took their property.
The Spirit commands Nephi to slay the man, saying the Lord has delivered him into Nephi’s hands.
The Spirit states that the Lord slays the wicked to bring forth righteous purposes, and that it is better for one man to perish than for a nation to dwindle and perish in unbelief.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is present as the Spirit speaks to him; the verses do not describe the Spirit’s appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: Setting and surroundings
How the Spirit’s words are represented visually
Nephi’s appearance, posture, and expression

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the man by name.
Do not specify a location.
Do not depict a slaying or invent a visible form for the Spirit.

title: Nephi remembers the commandments
summary: Nephi remembers the Lord’s words about his seed keeping the commandments and prospering in the land of promise. He thinks they need the law of Moses to keep the commandments, knows the law is engraved on the brass plates, and knows why the Lord delivered Laban into his hands.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi remembers the Lord’s words spoken to him in the wilderness: if his seed keep the Lord’s commandments, they will prosper in the land of promise.
Nephi thinks they cannot keep the Lord’s commandments according to the law of Moses unless they have the law.
Nephi knows the law is engraved upon the plates of brass.
Nephi knows the Lord delivered Laban into his hands so that he might obtain the records according to the Lord’s commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is reflecting; the verses do not establish a specific present location or action.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance and posture
Whether any plates or records are visible
The Lord’s appearance

narration.text: And now, when I, Nephi, had heard these words, I remembered the words of the Lord
they could not keep the commandments of the Lord according to the law of Moses
the law was engraven upon the plates of brass
the Lord had delivered Laban into my hands

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses narrate Nephi’s recollection and reasoning; they do not depict the remembered wilderness words or Laban’s delivery as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a separate wilderness event or an appearance of the Lord.
Do not invent a current setting, physical action, or visual depiction of Laban.

title: Nephi obeys the Spirit
summary: Nephi takes Laban by the hair and smites off his head with Laban’s sword. Afterward, Nephi takes Laban’s garments, puts them on, and girds on Laban’s armor.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi obeys the voice of the Spirit, takes Laban by the hair of the head, and smites off his head with his own sword.
Afterward, Nephi takes Laban’s garments, puts them on, and girds on Laban’s armor about his loins.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The explicitly described action can be depicted without gore; Nephi wears Laban’s garments and armor afterward.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the exact appearance of the garments, armor, and sword are unspecified.

narration.text: Therefore I did obey the voice of the Spirit

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The killing and subsequent change of clothing are sequential events; do not combine them into one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore, blood, or severed body parts.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Spirit.

title: Nephi approaches the treasury
summary: Nephi goes toward Laban’s treasury, sees Laban’s servant with the treasury keys, and commands him in Laban’s voice to go with him into the treasury. Seeing the garments and sword, the servant supposes Nephi is Laban.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi goes toward Laban’s treasury and sees Laban’s servant, who has its keys.
Nephi commands the servant in Laban’s voice to go with him into the treasury.
The servant supposes Nephi is Laban after seeing the garments and the sword girded about Nephi’s loins.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is wearing the garments seen by the servant.
The servant carries the treasury keys.
unspecified_visual_details: The treasury’s architecture and contents
Nephi’s and the servant’s appearance beyond the stated garments and sword
The servant’s exact position

narration.text: I saw the servant of Laban who had the keys of the treasury.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words of Nephi’s command; it is reported indirectly.
Do not depict Nephi as physically transformed into Laban.

title: The servant follows the narrator
summary: Laban’s servant speaks to the narrator about the elders of the Jews. The narrator speaks as if he were Laban, says he should carry the engravings on the brass plates to his elder brethren outside the walls, and bids the servant follow him. The servant supposes the narrator is Laban and follows him.

explicit_facts.text: The servant speaks to the narrator concerning the elders of the Jews and knows that Laban had been out among them by night.
The narrator speaks to him as if he were Laban.
The narrator says he should carry the engravings on the brass plates to his elder brethren, who are outside the walls.
The narrator bids him follow.
The servant supposes the narrator means the brethren of the church and is truly Laban, whom the narrator had slain; he follows the narrator.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The narrator and servant converse before the servant follows him.
unspecified_visual_details: The encounter’s exact location

Do not depict Laban, the elders, or the elder brethren as present in this encounter.

title: The brothers flee and stop
summary: As the narrator goes toward his brothers outside the walls, an unidentified man speaks to him many times concerning the elders of the Jews. Laman, Lemuel, and Sam see the narrator, become frightened, and flee, supposing he is Laban. The narrator calls after them; they hear him and stop fleeing.
characters: Unidentified man who speaks to the narrator

explicit_facts.text: An unidentified man spoke to the narrator many times concerning the elders of the Jews as the narrator went toward his brothers, who were outside the walls.
When Laman saw the narrator, Laman was exceedingly frightened; Lemuel and Sam were also frightened.
They fled because they supposed the narrator was Laban and supposed Laban had slain him and sought to take their lives.
The narrator called after them; they heard him and ceased fleeing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fleeing brothers come to a stop after hearing the narrator call.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of each person

title: An oath and an offer
summary: The speaker tells a man that they will spare his life if he hearkens to their words. Speaking with an oath, he says the man need not fear and can be free like them if he goes into the wilderness with them. He says the Lord commanded them and offers the man a place with them if he goes to the speaker’s father.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says they will spare the man’s life if he hearkens to their words.
Speaking with an oath, the speaker says the man need not fear and should be free like them if he goes into the wilderness with them.
The speaker says the Lord commanded them to do this thing and offers the man a place with them if he goes into the wilderness to the speaker’s father.

summary: Zoram takes courage at Nephi’s words, promises to go into the wilderness to their father, and swears to remain with them. They desire his company so the Jews will not learn of their flight and pursue them. After Zoram makes the oath, their fears concerning him cease.

explicit_facts.text: Zoram is the servant’s name; he takes courage at the words Nephi spoke, promises to go into the wilderness to their father, and makes an oath to remain with them from then on.
They desire Zoram to remain with them so the Jews will not learn of their flight into the wilderness, pursue them, and destroy them.
After Zoram makes an oath to them, their fears concerning him cease.
